source: 1968 Chevrolet Chassis Service Manual, Clutch and Transmissions, p.7-34

procedures.title: Turbo Hydra-Matic: general description
notes: Selecting L2 at speed shifts to second and stays there until speed or throttle bring first gear as in Drive.
L1 can be selected at any speed: the transmission goes to second and stays until speed drops to about 40 MPH (depends on axle ratio), then holds first and will not upshift.

Any correspondence about a Turbo Hydra-Matic must quote the transmission serial number and the Vehicle Identification number; parts returned to Chevrolet must be tagged with the transmission serial number.

procedures.title: Turbo Hydra-Matic fluid level check
steps: Check the fluid with the transmission warm and the selector in Park, each time engine oil is checked or as given in Section 0 at engine oil changes.
Change the fluid at the Section 0 interval.
notes: The dipstick FULL mark reads correctly only at the normal operating temperature of 180°F, which takes at least 15 miles of expressway driving or the equivalent in town.

procedures.title: Turbo Hydra-Matic detent switch adjustment (Corvette)
steps: Line up the hole in the switch driver with the hole in the switch and push a .092 pin in .10" deep to lock the driver.
Move the accelerator lever to wide open throttle, making sure the accelerator linkage is adjusted correctly first.
Mount the switch loosely on its bracket and slide it toward the lever until the driver touches the lever.
Tighten the bolt holding the switch to the bracket, then pull the pin.
notes: The Corvette uses the accelerator-lever-mounted switch shown in figure 1T in the manual; the carburetor plunger switch with dimension A applies to other car lines.
